svg.title: A startup operating model used small AI-enabled pods to launch a healthcare portal in one month and parallelize the remaining portfolio
svg.desc: Anonymous healthcare and life sciences case study showing how a 12-person scrum team became four three-person outcome pods using executable specifications, embedded controls and reusable delivery assets.
svg.text: Startup delivery model for a five-portal portfolio
A 12-person scrum team became four AI-enabled mini-pods working from executable product specifications

text.tspan: only one portal at a time

svg.text: The five-portal queue exceeded the market window
Handoffs separated domain, build and quality work
Every portal repeated the setup effort
Requirements and controls had to be rebuilt
Requirements, acceptance rules and controls stayed linked through release
Each pod combined domain, engineering and quality ownership
Proved the model, then ran portals in parallel
The first pod shipped in one month and the pattern moved to the portfolio
PEOPLE IN THE ORIGINAL SCRUM TEAM
Small outcome pods multiplied portfolio speed while executable specifications kept delivery in control
